title: From Superficial Outputs to Superficial Learning: Risks of Large Language Models in Education

bias_targets.methodology: Synthesizing studies that evaluate LLM grading behavior, feedback, and academic recommendations using counterfactual prompts with varied racial and ethnic demographic profiles (e.g., Black, White, Asian, Hispanic).
Reviewing experimental studies that test LLM scoring and personalized content delivery by altering cues related to income level, social class, parental education, and school type.

Synthesizing research that evaluates stereotyping in LLM-generated images of professionals (e.g., chemists, medical students) and analyzes institutional data for algorithmic fairness in student progress monitoring.
Reviewing algorithmic audits that examine disparities in personalized educational content and student progress prediction algorithms based on disability status and special education classifications.

Synthesizing qualitative and linguistic analyses to identify WEIRD (Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, Democratic) cultural assumptions and Anglocentric tendencies in LLM-generated narratives and instructional materials.
Reviewing sociolinguistic evaluations of LLM outputs to measure alignment with dominant white linguistic norms and raciolinguistic ideologies.

Synthesizing experimental studies that measure shifts in users' perceptions and cognitive processing of different world religions (e.g., Christianity, Judaism, Islam) after exposure to LLM-generated content.
Reviewing studies that evaluate demographic disparities in LLM-generated college major recommendations for LGBTQ users compared to heterosexual users.
Synthesizing findings from algorithmic fairness evaluations that track student trajectories and progress monitoring based on institutional age data.
